newsitem.title: USA: Case sets $3.4 billion credit facility.
newsitem.headline: Case sets $3.4 billion credit facility.

text.p: Case Corp said Tuesday it established $3.4 billion in lines of credit and liquidity facilities, the majority of which are assigned to Case Credit.
As a result, Case said it will take an $11 million or $0.15 a share extraordinary, after-tax charge in the third quarter for unamortized bank fees related to the original bank agreements.
The new facilities replace borrowing agreements originally arranged at the time of the company's initial public offering in June 1994 and amended last year.
The new agreements were negotiated at more favorable rates and terms for the company, Case said.

Of the $3.4 billion total, $2.3 billion of the credit facilities will benefit Case Credit and its Canadian subsidiary. The unit plans to continue to grow its business by broadening its product offerings to meet the financing needs of its customers, Case said.

Case Credit launched a new credit card program this year for dealer-based purchases and, in 1995, expanded into Australia. Under the new agreements, Case will continue to maintain a support agreement to Case Credit relative to ownership and financial backing.
"These agreements will support our growth strategies, while both lowering our borrowing costs and increasing our operating flexibility," Jean-Pierre Rosso, chairman, said in a statement.
Case, with net sales of nearly $5 billion in 1995, makes agricultural and construction equipment.
